newsitem.title: INDIA: WPP's O&M India buys 80 pct of Speer - paper.
newsitem.headline: WPP's O&M India buys 80 pct of Speer - paper.

text.p: NEW DELHI, June 5 (REUTER) - Ogilvy & Mather India (O&M), the country's third largest advertising agency, has taken an 80 percent state in Bombay-based Speer Advertising, the Business Standard newspaper reported on Saturday.
It said the remaining 20 percent was retained by Speer.
Business Standard said Speer's billings amounted to 200 million rupees ($5.5 million) in 1996/97.
The U.S. based Advertising Age reported last month that Ogilvy & Mather India had capitalised billings of $88.2 million in 1996/97.
"I have been looking for a partner of international stature and creative compatibility. O&M offers both of these," Sajid Peerbhoy, Speer's founder, was quoted as saying.
The report did not mention the price paid by O&M for its stake in Speer.
Ogilvy and Mather Worldwide, part of Britain's advertising and marketing concern WPP Group, has a 51 percent stake in O&M India.
WPP has stakes in three other agencies in India including the country's largest, Hindustan Thompson Associates. It also has stakes in Contract and Equus.
